Equivalent: For each index i, we have two possible values: a[i] = nums1[i], b[i] = nums2[i]. We want to assign each index a value (choose one of two) to maximize the length of the longest contiguous subarray where assigned values are non-decreasing.

We need to compute maximum possible length of a subarray [l, r] where we can assign values from each position to satisfy non-decreasing condition.

This looks like a DP problem similar to longest increasing subsequence with two choices per position, but we need contiguous subarray.

Observation: For a given subarray, we need to know if there exists a choice assignment such that the sequence is non-decreasing. Equivalent to: there exists a sequence of choices c[i] ∈ {0,1} (0 picks nums1[i], 1 picks nums2[i]) such that for all i from l to r-1, chosen[i] <= chosen[i+1].

We can think of DP that tracks, for each position i, the longest valid subarray ending at i, given we chose either nums1[i] or nums2[i] at i. This is similar to computing longest non-decreasing subarray when each element has two possible values. We want maximum length over any ending index and choice.

Define dp0[i] = length of longest non-decreasing subarray ending at i if we choose nums1[i] at position i.
Similarly dp1[i] = length if we choose nums2[i] at position i.

Transition: dp0[i] = 1 + max over possible previous choice j in {0,1} such that chosen value at i-1 <= nums1[i]; i.e., if nums1[i-1] <= nums1[i] then we can extend dp0[i-1]; if nums2[i-1] <= nums1[i] then we can extend dp1[i-1]; dp0[i] = 1 + max of those applicable previous dp values; if none applicable then dp0[i] = 1 (starting new subarray at i). Similarly dp1[i] based on nums2[i].

Then answer = max over i and both dp values.
